question: Should OpenClaw adopt this opt-in core durable-recovery contract, including the `durable` configuration surface and shared-state recovery coordination, or keep recovery within existing owner-specific paths?
rationale: The PR is a broad new runtime and persistence boundary, not a repair of an established contract; code review cannot determine whether its long-term core ownership, operational burden, and public configuration surface match maintainer product direction.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core durable contract
options.body: Approve the owner-first recovery boundary, then require a current-main rebase and explicit upgrade and operational contract before merging the implementation slices.

options.title: Keep recovery owner-specific
options.body: Decline the shared durable layer and ask for narrowly demonstrated fixes in the existing task, flow, subagent, and session owners instead.

options.title: Move the proposal to an RFC first
options.body: Keep the implementation paused until maintainers accept or narrow the linked architecture proposal and define the intended release sequence.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core durable contract
recommendation.body: Approve the owner-first recovery boundary, then require a current-main rebase and explicit upgrade and operational contract before merging the implementation slices.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor has the clearest context for the proposed durable-stack boundary and can respond to a maintainer sponsorship or narrowing decision.
